title: Shortcuts: Triangular, Row-Sum, All-Ones and Rank-One Matrices
quickIdea: Recognising structure beats expanding a determinant: a triangular matrix reads its eigenvalues off the diagonal, a constant row sum is an eigenvalue, and J - I has n-1 once and -1 with multiplicity n-1.
remember: Triangular or diagonal: the eigenvalues are exactly the diagonal entries, repeated as often as they appear.
If every row of A sums to c then c is an eigenvalue with eigenvector (1,1,...,1); the same holds for columns.
The all-ones matrix J of order n has eigenvalues n once and 0 with multiplicity n-1, because its rank is 1.
J - I therefore has eigenvalues n-1 once and -1 with multiplicity n-1. For n = 4 that is 3, -1, -1, -1.
A rank-one matrix u v^T has eigenvalues v^T u once and 0 with multiplicity n-1.
0 is an eigenvalue exactly when det A = 0; 1 is an eigenvalue exactly when det(A - I) = 0.

example.prompt: Find the largest eigenvalue of the 4x4 matrix with 0 on the diagonal and 1 everywhere else.
example.work: The matrix is J - I with n = 4. Every row sums to 3, so 3 is an eigenvalue with eigenvector (1,1,1,1). J has rank 1 and trace 4, so its eigenvalues are 4, 0, 0, 0; subtracting I shifts each one by -1, giving 3, -1, -1, -1. The trace check holds: 3 - 1 - 1 - 1 = 0 = trace(J - I).
example.answer: The eigenvalues are 3, -1, -1, -1, so the largest is 3, the answer to GATE CSE 2021 Set 1 Q.52.

gateAngle: 2021 Set 1 Q.52 is J - I and is one line once the structure is seen. 2014 Set 2 Q.47 has rank 2 and trace 5, and the two nonzero eigenvalues are pinned by trace(A^2) = 13, giving 2 and 3 and a product of 6. Both are structure questions, not expansion questions.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Every row of a 5x5 matrix sums to 4. Name one eigenvalue and one eigenvector.
variations.why: A(1,...,1)^T has i-th entry equal to the sum of row i, which is 4, so the all-ones vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 4.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does a rank-one matrix u v^T have n-1 eigenvalues equal to 0?
variations.answer: Its image is the single line spanned by u, so its null space has dimension n-1, which is the geometric multiplicity of the eigenvalue 0.
variations.why: The remaining eigenvalue is the trace, v^T u, because the trace is the sum of all eigenvalues and the other n-1 are zero.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A = J - I of order 5. What is det A?
variations.why: The eigenvalues are 4 once and -1 four times, so the determinant is 4 x (-1)^4 = 4. The count of -1 eigenvalues is n-1 = 4, which is even here, so the sign is positive.

trap.what: Reading the eigenvalues off the diagonal of a matrix that is not triangular.
trap.why: The diagonal-reading rule depends on the matrix being triangular, which makes the characteristic determinant a product of diagonal terms; without that structure the off-diagonal entries change the roots.
trap.counterexample: A = [[1,2],[3,4]] has diagonal entries 1 and 4, but its eigenvalues are (5 + sqrt33)/2 and (5 - sqrt33)/2, about 5.372 and -0.372.

check.question: A is 4x4 and rank one, of the form u v^T with v^T u = 7. What are its eigenvalues?
check.explanation: The trace is v^T u = 7, the nullity is 3, so one eigenvalue is 7 and the other three are 0. The sum 7 matches the trace, which is the check.
